To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the elliptic flow of heavy quarks in the 0-30% centrality Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200$~GeV is consistent with a mass scaling of light flavor mesons; and (ii) the di-electron production in Au+Au collisions shows an enhancement over the expected yield from known sources.

(1) the heavy quark transport coefficient in Au-Au collisions is consistent with the value in p+p collisions, and (2) the elliptic flow of electrons from heavy flavor decays in Au-Au collision is consistent with the hydrodynamical model.

the study of the hot and dense medium created in the relativistic nuclear collisions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heavy quark probes provide strong evidence for a strongly interacting QGP.
the heavy flavor and electron production measurements are consistent with a strongly interacting quark-gluon plasma.

the heavy flavor production is consistent with a picture in which heavy quarks are produced in the early stages of the collisions, and are modified by the interaction with the hot and dense medium, but not completely thermalized.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the STAR measurements of heavy quark production and di-electron are consistent with a scenario where the medium created in the relativistic nuclear collisions is a strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma (sQGP).

we have obtained the first measurement of the heavy flavor contribution to single electron spectra in heavy ion collisions at the top RHIC energy, and we have obtained the highest precision measurement of single electron production from charm decays in p+p collisions, which provides a baseline for heavy ion results.
we have observed the suppression of heavy flavor production in central collisions, while the suppression factor is smaller than the one observed for light flavor production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
heavy flavor and di-elecron measurements at STAR are consistent with a strong coupling to the medium, which is consistent with the formation of a quark-gluon plasma.
we are now able to measure heavy flavor production in a broad kinematic range at STAR and to investigate the heavy flavor interactions with the medium.
the heavy quark energy loss is large in Au+Au and Cu+Au collisions, which is consistent with the large suppression of heavy flavor meson production.
